title: 2017 Body Shots - Analyzing Shooting Styles in the NBA using Body-Pose Attributes
file_name: 2017 Body Shots - Analyzing Shooting Styles in the NBA using Body-Pose Attributes.pdf
universal_lens: Body-pose kinematics unify shooting style analysis through 3D trajectory inference, enabling objective form evaluation beyond SportVU x,y,z coordinates. Temporal binning of NBA shooting actions maps kinematic phases to pose attributes via skeletal tracking.
gsi_mapping: GSI employs conformal predictive distributions over 3D body pose trajectories to quantify shooting form uncertainty, mapping observed kinematics to probabilistic performance forecasts. Bayesian inference on shot outcome conditioned on body-pose bins uses conformal prediction for uncertainty quantification.
gse_mapping: GSE models situational state transitions using pose-based action recognition kernels, inferring optimal shooting windows from defender proximity and player balance dynamics. Situationally-aware state transitions model player motion through five-phase timeline using derived kinematic kernels.

primitives.name: Pose Trajectory Inference
primitives.verbatim_quote: Objective measures, requisite for meaningful comparisons, demand trajectories of players' 3D body pose.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'p(t)': 'player pose at time t, dimensionless', 'T': 'trajectory duration, seconds'}
primitives.assumptions: Player pose is captured via 3D skeletal tracking with temporal resolution sufficient for dynamic form analysis.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When body-pose data is unavailable, form comparison becomes subjective and non-reproducible.

layer2.mapping: Pose trajectory kernel maps 3D joint positions to shooting form metrics via dynamic time warping and principal component analysis.
layer2.telemetry: Joint angle variance across shooting cycle, normalized by player height.

primitives.name: Shooting Form Quantification
primitives.verbatim_quote: The value of such player pose information is expansive, from predicting movements to quantifying the ideal pose for a movement.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'F(p)': 'form score of pose p, dimensionless', 'p_{ideal}': 'ideal pose configuration, dimensionless'}
primitives.assumptions: Ideal form is defined as minimal deviation from a canonical shooting posture under given biomechanical constraints.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Form quantification fails when pose data lacks sufficient joint resolution or temporal granularity.

layer2.mapping: Form quantification is isomorphic to a Riemannian manifold projection onto a canonical shooting posture space.
layer2.telemetry: Cosine similarity between actual and ideal pose vectors.

primitives.name: Kinematic Opportunity Assessment
primitives.verbatim_quote: And why does he wait until his defender has closed-out before shooting?
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'K(t)': 'kinematic opportunity at time t, dimensionless', 'd(t)': 'defender distance at time t, meters', 'v(t)': 'player velocity at time t, m/s'}
primitives.assumptions: Opportunity assessment depends on relative motion and spatial alignment between player and defender.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Assessment invalid when defender motion is not accounted for or when player is off-balance.

layer2.mapping: Opportunity kernel combines defender proximity and player momentum into a scalar utility function.
layer2.telemetry: Time-to-contact threshold crossing rate during shooting window.

primitives.name: Balance Dynamics Model
primitives.verbatim_quote: From SportVU data alone, this appears to be a very high-percentage opportunity.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'B(t)': 'balance state at time t, dimensionless', 'C(t)': 'center-of-mass trajectory at time t, meters', 'σ(t)': 'variance in CoM displacement, m²'}
primitives.assumptions: Balance is inferred from center-of-mass stability during shooting execution.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Model fails when SportVU data lacks CoM tracking or when external forces disrupt equilibrium.

layer2.mapping: Balance dynamics model is isomorphic to a stochastic control process over CoM variance.
layer2.telemetry: Standard deviation of CoM path during shot preparation phase.

primitives.name: Temporal Bin Framework
primitives.verbatim_quote: Wedividedthetime-lineofashotinto󰅭ivebins: (blue)beforetheplayerpossessestheball, (pink)when the player possesses the ball before the shot, (black) immediately before the shot, (green) during the jump and release, and (red) after the player lands.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'t': 'time in seconds', 'B': 'bin index {1,2,3,4,5}', 'T_B': 'duration of bin B'}
primitives.assumptions: Shot timeline is segmented into discrete temporal bins with fixed duration; each bin corresponds to a unique biomechanical phase.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When t < 0 or t > T_total, binning becomes undefined due to lack of relevant kinematic data.

layer2.mapping: Each temporal bin maps to a distinct pose feature vector in GSE's kinematic kernel space.
layer2.telemetry: Pose extraction accuracy per bin via skeleton tracking confidence scores.

primitives.name: Kinematic Pose Attribute Set
primitives.verbatim_quote: For each bin, we record attributes designed to capture the variety of movements the shooter may take, at different levels of granularity, from the direction of their full body movements to the foot they step with immediately before their shot.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'A_{B}': 'attribute set for bin B', 'D_{body}': 'direction of full-body movement (dimensionless)', 'F_{step}': 'foot used for step (left/right/hop)'}
primitives.assumptions: Attributes are independent variables capturing movement variability across bins; granularity varies from global to local.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When A_B is empty or undefined due to occlusion or tracking failure.

layer2.mapping: Pose attributes define a feature kernel in GSE's action recognition manifold.
layer2.telemetry: Average precision of pose classification per attribute type.

primitives.name: High-Level Shot Anatomy
primitives.verbatim_quote: They set their feet, grasp the ball with their hands, jump and/or extend into the air, release the ball toward the basket, and land back on the 󰅭loor.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'S': 'shot sequence', 'F_{set}': 'feet positioning', 'H_{grasp}': 'hand grip strength (N)', 'J_{jump}': 'jump height (m)', 'R_{release}': 'release trajectory vector (m/s)', 'L_{land}': 'landing stability (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Shot anatomy consists of sequential biomechanical actions; each action contributes to overall shot efficacy.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When S lacks one or more defined actions (e.g., no jump or release).

layer2.mapping: High-level shot actions map to GSI's probabilistic shot success model.
layer2.telemetry: Success rate of shots with complete anatomical sequences.

primitives.name: Balance Attribute
primitives.verbatim_quote: Outside of these designated bins, we include one additional attribute for overall balance during the full time-line of the shot.
primitives.assumptions: Overall balance is a scalar measure of postural control throughout the shot execution.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When B_overall cannot be computed due to missing pose data or instability.

layer2.mapping: Balance attribute forms part of GSE's dynamic stability kernel.
layer2.telemetry: Correlation between B_overall and shot accuracy metrics.

primitives.name: Chi-Squared Shot Classification
primitives.verbatim_quote: To quantify these differences, for each of these four cases, we perform a Pearson's Chi-squared test on the histograms for each attribute.
primitives.assumptions: Data follows categorical distribution; independence of observations; expected frequency > 5 per cell.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When p-value < 0.1, significant difference in attribute distributions between shot classes.

layer2.mapping: Chi-squared test outputs map to GSI's Bayesian belief updates on shot type likelihood given observed pose features.

primitives.name: Pose Attribute Distribution Shift
primitives.verbatim_quote: A visual inspection indicates clear differences between the attribute distributions, especially with movement before and after a shot.
primitives.assumptions: Attribute values are independently sampled; histogram bins are sufficiently populated.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Shifts exceed threshold variance in mean or entropy between shot types.

layer2.mapping: Distribution shift metrics inform GSE's kernel density estimation of player-specific shooting behavior kernels.
layer2.telemetry: Histogram overlap coefficients and Kullback-Leibler divergence measures.

primitives.name: Statistical Significance Threshold
primitives.verbatim_quote: For many attributes, the difference in distributions between shot classes is statistically signi󰅭icant at an α = 0.1 signi󰅭icance level for at least one set of shot comparisons.
primitives.assumptions: Null hypothesis of no difference holds under standard parametric assumptions.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When p < 0.1, reject null hypothesis of equal distribution.

layer2.mapping: Threshold-based rejection criteria align with GSI's conformal prediction confidence bands for shot classification.
layer2.telemetry: Binary flags indicating statistical significance of attribute differences.

primitives.name: Curry Shooting Style Signature
primitives.verbatim_quote: Individual tests for each attribute enables us to see exactly which attributes exhibit statistically signi󰅭icant differences between the shot classes.
primitives.assumptions: Curry's off-balance shots are representative of his overall shooting profile; comparative baseline is valid.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Exceeds baseline mean balance proportion by >1σ.

layer2.mapping: Signature vector defines GSE's reference kernel for Curry’s unique shooting state-space trajectory.
layer2.telemetry: Normalized frequency vectors of key pose attributes for Curry vs. others.

primitives.name: Temporal Pose Binning
primitives.verbatim_quote: We divided the time-line of a shot into 󰅭ive bins: (blue) before the player possesses the ball, (pink) when the player possesses the ball before the shot, (black) immediately before the shot, (green) during the jump and release, and (red) after the player lands.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'t': 'time in seconds', 'B': 'bin index ∈ {1,2,3,4,5}', 'T_B': 'duration of bin B'}
primitives.assumptions: Shot trajectory is segmented into discrete temporal phases with distinct kinematic signatures.
primitives.breakdown_regime: At t = 0 (ball possession start), t = T (shot release), and t = T+Δt (landing).

layer2.mapping: Each temporal bin maps to a unique pose feature vector in GSI's attribute space, enabling conformal prediction of shot success.
layer2.telemetry: Pose keypoint coordinates per bin for shot classification.

primitives.name: Pose Attribute Space
primitives.verbatim_quote: Summary In this work, we have introduced a novel, attribute-based representation for a shooter's body pose.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'A': 'attribute vector in ℝ^n', 'n': 'number of pose descriptors', 'p_i': 'i-th pose parameter (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Body pose can be represented as a set of measurable geometric attributes.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When p_i exceeds measurement threshold or falls below noise floor.

layer2.mapping: Attribute space defines kernel similarity between shots, used in GSE for pattern recognition.
layer2.telemetry: Cosine similarity between A(t) vectors across shots.

primitives.name: Shot Outcome Classifier
primitives.verbatim_quote: We demonstrated the value of this pose representation by showing how a shooter's attributes differ for made and missed shots in different game contexts.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'C(A)': 'classifier function mapping A → {made, missed}', 'P(made|A)': 'probability of made shot given pose attributes', 'P(missed|A)': 'probability of missed shot given pose attributes'}
primitives.assumptions: Conditional independence of attributes given shot outcome under fixed game context.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When P(made|A) ≈ P(missed|A) or when A is undefined.

layer2.mapping: Classifier output in GSI corresponds to GSE decision node for shot execution.
layer2.telemetry: Log-likelihood ratio of made vs missed shot predictions.

primitives.name: Curry Shot Style Analysis
primitives.verbatim_quote: And, we performed one case study using our attribute representation on Stephen Curry's shooting style.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'S_C': "Stephen Curry's shot style profile", 'μ_A': 'mean attribute vector for S_C', 'Σ_A': 'covariance matrix of attributes for S_C'}
primitives.assumptions: Curry’s shooting style exhibits consistent attribute distribution across shots.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When μ_A deviates beyond 2σ confidence interval of baseline.

layer2.mapping: Style kernel in GSE encodes Curry-specific pose patterns for tactical modeling.
layer2.telemetry: KL divergence between S_C and general shooter profiles.
